front.title: FTP Error Code Usage for More Reliable Mail Service

section.name: PURPOSE
section.t: A major hindrance to providing reliable mail service is the lack of well-defined FTP error replies that would enable a mailing process to decide how to handle a failure. New FTP error codes are currently in the design stage, and a proposal will be announced soon. In the interim, we can get some improvement by simply defining how we intend to use the current FTP codes. The purpose of this RFC is to inform all sites of how TENEX sites will use and interpret the codes starting in the near future.

section.name: CURRENT CODE DEFINITIONS
section.t: The FTP error codes defined for failure to perform a file action (including mail) are:

dl.dd: Cannot connect to your data socket

section.t: 450, 451, and 453 are applicable to both the MAIL and MLFL commands, while 452 and 454 are only meaningful for MLFL.

section.name: SHORTCOMING OF CURRENT DEFINITIONS
section.t: There are more possible causes of failure to deliver mail than the ones defined above. Implementors of FTP servers thus had to make arbitrary assignments of error conditions to defined codes. As a result, although the text of the reply might distinguish these conditions for the benefit of human users, the code doesn't distinguish them for the benefit of processes.

The minimum distinction needed by the TENEX mail-sending processes is between permanent and non-permanent failures. In the latter case, the process will repeatedly try to deliver the mail for several days.

section.name: NEW DEFINITIONS FOR TENEX USE
section.t: The following changes will be installed at TENEX sites over the next couple of months.

section.name: FTP SERVER
section.t: The TENEX FTP server will continue to use 452 and 454 as specified for the MLFL command.
For MAIL and MLFL, it will send the other codes as follows:

dd.t: Permanent failures due to the user addressed in the Mail or MLFL command.
Examples: No such user; No mailbox for that user; Can't access file (because net users can't write in that mailbox).
Permanent failures due to the message itself.
Example: Line sent over TELNET connection is too long (MAIL command only).
Examples: TELNET connection unexpectedly closed; Mailbox busy; Unexpected local errors (such as failure to create scratch file).

section.name: MAILING PROCESSES
section.t: TENEX mailing processes currently interpret all the codes 450-454 as meaning permanent failure. They will be changed to interpret 452, 453, and 454 as temporary while leaving 450 and 451 permanent.

section.name: COMPATIBILITY WITH NON-TENEX SITES
section.t: These interpretations should not adversely affect the interaction of TENEX and non-TENEX mail processes, since we are simply changing from one arbitrary set of interpretations to another. Moreover:

ul.li: Our interpretation of 450-451 as permanent and 452-454 as temporary is consistent with their original meanings.
Our new choice of what codes to use for what failure is no farther from the original meanings than our old choice was, and conveys more information.
